A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProReason research work. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, LLM-assisted evaluations, sub-agent analyses, and token-consumption measurements, including Tables 4–12.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds A-OKVQA evaluation, agent-merging experiments, retry-budget tests, response-quality assessments, and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the prescribed fallback: v1 summarizes after five unsuccessful expert calls; v2 clears Memory and restarts acquisition, allowing five attempts before summarizing. This modifies inference while retaining the five-agent architecture. Regrouping Action, Judgment, and Summary into two named phases mainly changes the explanation.

E1.justification: V2 adds conventional knowledge-based visual question answering on A-OKVQA (Appendix A.3.3, Table 5). MME cognition tasks, MMMU, MathVista, and HallusionBench remain, making this a limited extension of dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Direct, VDGD, CCoT, CoT, and ReAct remain the peer baselines; A-OKVQA reuses that set. V2 adds three internal comparison variants merging two, four, or all five ProReason agents (Table 13). These are evaluated ablation comparators rather than new external baselines.

E3.justification: Beyond the revised restart budget in Section 4.1, v2 introduces agent-merging controls and tests allowances of one, three, and five attempts. Its new response-quality study uses GPT-4o reference answers and relevance, redundancy, and missing-information ratings (Appendix A.3.4). The original preliminary evaluation remains. Together these substantially expand the evaluation design without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct tests of decoupling through agent consolidation, sensitivity to retry allowances, assessments of Memory and Summarizer information quality, expert-selection frequencies, and clock/geometry failure cases. These substantially extend the existing sub-agent substitution and capability-importance analyses, which are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's one/three/five-attempt experiments vary inference retries; they do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for A-OKVQA, consolidation, retries, response quality, and expert-call frequency. From v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 1, LLaVA's MMMU score changes from 52.5 to 50.5, while GPT-4o-mini's MME and HallusionBench scores change from 90.4 to 91.9 and 58.9 to 59.9. These are reported revisions under a changed retry rule, not established same-setting gains. Older values persist elsewhere; v2 Table 14 also changes the displayed MME scale without explanation. V2 Table 5 reports A-OKVQA scores of 81.3 versus Direct's 78.9, inconsistent with its printed +2.7.

T1.justification: The symbolic method description involving the image, question, expert queries, and stored answers remains equivalent. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the added empirical analyses introduce no substantive mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: proactive information acquisition, decoupled perception and reasoning, superiority over passive and multi-step methods, and LLM-assisted visual reasoning. The headline improvements of 13.2% and up to 15% remain. Added decoupling experiments support an existing claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning propagation of visual errors and agents' failure to challenge earlier information, motivating reflection (Section 6). New interpretations attribute hallucination filtering to the Referee, describe a redundancy-versus-information-loss tradeoff in Memory, and connect expert-call frequency with task difficulty. These considerably expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository link and code-release statement, a CUDA/NVIDIA A100 deployment note, and prompt templates for the new response assessment and three consolidation configurations (Figures 12–15). The original agent and baseline prompts remain. These are additional disclosures; repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Schwenk et al. (2022) for A-OKVQA and Ji et al. (2023) for self-reflection. The existing related-work discussion and positioning against passive visual extraction and LLM reasoning frameworks remain substantially intact, relocated to Appendix A.1.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the method is rewritten around two phases, related work and dataset descriptions move into the appendix, and the former Section 4.4 becomes Appendix A.3.1 while a new decoupling section takes its place. Limitations and Ethics sections are added, alongside introduction edits and an expanded author list.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from single-column to predominantly two-column layout, redraws Figure 1 to emphasize the two phases, relocates preliminary and ablation tables, and transposes several retained tables. It also adds analysis tables, a fuller display of the existing wire example, failure-case figures, and new prompt panels.

improvement.justification: The consolidation experiments, information-quality analyses, and explicit failure discussion improve support for the proposed mechanism and expose limitations absent from v1. Additional prompts also aid reproducibility. The net gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: v2 Table 1 gives LLaVA MMMU as 50.5 while Table 3 retains 52.5, Table 5 contains an incorrect improvement calculation, and revised retry settings are not reconciled across retained results and costs. These problems limit confidence in the expanded evidence.
